label: Oil stays at today's level
description: Brent stays at the October 2026 level (about $111) instead of following the backwardated futures curve (about $95 in 2027, $75 in 2029).

label: Oil +30% above the futures curve (persistent)
description: Brent 30% above the baseline curve from 2026Q4 and for the whole horizon: about one standard deviation of annual Brent changes, a persistent supply loss.

label: Oil 30% below the futures curve (persistent)
description: Mirror image: Brent 30% below the baseline curve from 2026Q4 (demand slowdown or supply recovery).

label: Temporary oil spike in 2027 (+50%, fading)
description: A new supply disruption: Brent 50% above the curve in 2027Q1-Q2, fading linearly to the curve over the next four quarters.

label: Oil normalises quickly to $70
description: Brent falls linearly from $111 to $70 by June 2027 and stays there (the pre-spike range was $62-71): the spike is reversed faster than the market curve implies.

label: Oil follows the EIA STEO path
description: Brent follows the EIA Short-Term Energy Outlook of the pull (about $95 in 2027Q1, $74 in 2027Q4) and then the futures curve's month-to-month changes: below the futures curve.

label: Labour market tightens (V/U back to its 2019Q4 level)
description: V/U rises by 0.17 over four quarters, from 1.02 to 1.19, its 2019Q4 value, and stays: a demand-led tightening.

label: Labour market cools (V/U falls by 0.2)
description: V/U falls by 0.2 over four quarters, from 1.02 to 0.82, and stays.

label: Supply-chain pressure (GSCPI +1.0, persistent)
description: GSCPI 1.0 above baseline from 2026Q4, decaying with rho = 0.8 (half-life about 3 quarters): one standard deviation of GSCPI, a renewed but not extreme disruption.

label: Food prices +8% (nominal, permanent)
description: Nominal CPI food 8% above its baseline path, reached over four quarters and kept (the baseline path rises with wages).

label: Productivity growth 1 pp lower for two years
description: Trend productivity growth lower by 1 pp (annualised) in 2026Q4-2028Q3: slower supply growth.

label: Expectations de-anchor (1y +0.5 pp, 10y +0.2 pp)
description: A shock of +0.5 pp to one-year expected inflation in each of the next four quarters (not cumulated: the equation is persistent) and +0.05 pp per quarter to ten-year expectations: a structural risk scenario; the shock is to the expectations equations, not to a driver.

label: Adverse supply bundle
description: Oil +30% (persistent), GSCPI +1.0 (decaying), productivity growth 1 pp lower for two years.

label: Benign bundle (disinflation)
drivers: Oil / energy; Supply chains (GSCPI); Labour market (V/U)
description: Oil normalises quickly to $70, V/U falls by 0.2, GSCPI 0.5 below baseline throughout.

label: Overheating bundle (demand-led, oil stays high)
drivers: Oil / energy; Labour market (V/U); Expectations / price / wage shocks
description: V/U back to 1.19, oil stays at the October level, expectations drift up (as in the de-anchoring scenario).
